To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the 4-B(8)8/E9 antibody recognizes the gibberellin hormone GA(4) with a high affinity.

a monoclonal anti-gibberellic acid (GA) antibody, 4B8(8)/ E9 Fab, has a small hapten-combing site which is composed of three heavy chain complementarity-determining region loops, and the GA molecule is in van der Waal contact mainly with the side chain of the aromatic residue Tyr100A and Phe100B of CDR-H2 and H3, respectively.
the 4-B(8)/E(9) antibody recognizes the C/D rings of GA(4) in the C/D rings-combining site.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the crystal structure of the ligand-binding site of an anti-GA antibody.
the structural basis for the GA(4)-specific recognition by 4-B8 (8)/E9 antibody.
the crystal structure of the ligand-bound antibody 4-B 8(8)/ E9 Fab fragment, which was determined at a 2 8 A resolution by X-ray crystallography.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GA(4)-binding site of the 4B8(8)/9E Fab fragment is formed mainly by the heavy chain CDR-H3 loop and the heavy chain residues of CDR-H2 and CDR-H1, and that this binding site is a small pocket.
the 4-B(8)(8)/E9 anti-GA(4) antibody recognizes the GA(4)-binding site in the receptor protein.
the GA(4)/4-B8( 8)/E9 complex structure was determined for the first time and that the GA( 4)/4-B(8)/E(9) antibody complex structure was determined at 2.8-A resolution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the antibody recognizes GA(4) through its 3 beta-hydryl and 6 beta- carboxyl groups.
the 4-B(8)/E(9) Fab structure provides a basis to understand the GA(4)-binding mechanism of the antibody.
GA(4) binds to the antibody in a manner which is different from the binding of the ligand to the protein receptor, and the antibody is a useful tool in the study of GA(4) binding to the receptor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GA(4)-binding site is located at the C-terminal end of the heavy chain CDR-H3 loop.
the antibody can be used to study the binding of GA(4) with a receptor.
the 4-B88/E9 antibody has a small and unique GA(4)-combining site that recognizes a small molecule of GA(4) with a low affinity.
